# (real names; written from the English script). tools/storymap.py reads it.

column4: summary
Back from Mexico, Misawa is handed Tiger Mask's mask by Baba, then recalls his sudden debut against his senior Koshinaka.
Misawa's debut match against Koshinaka; a win adds 1 to the story score, but either result continues the story.
Misawa barely remembers his debut; two years of undercard matches later, he and Koshinaka head off to tour Mexico.
Living on fight money in Mexico, Koshinaka asks whether Misawa wants to go and eat some rice.
Misawa admits he's hungry and Koshinaka drags him to a pricey Japanese restaurant (+1 score).
Misawa tries to save money, but Koshinaka drags him to a Japanese restaurant anyway (no score).
Misawa and Koshinaka vow to come home as champions, until Baba suddenly recalls Misawa alone and tells him he is Tiger Mask.
Misawa must decide whether to accept becoming the second Tiger Mask.
Misawa accepts the mask (+3 score), proves his doubters wrong and challenges junior champion Kobayashi, the Tiger Hunter, for his title.
Misawa refuses the mask, Baba lets it go, and Jumbo sets up a heavyweight test match against Tenryu.
As Tiger Mask, Misawa challenges Kobayashi for the junior heavyweight title; a win adds 1 to the score.
Misawa's first big heavyweight match, against Tenryu; a win adds 1 to the score.
Kobayashi keeps his title and boasts no Tiger gets his belt; Misawa vows to grow from the loss.
Tiger Mask wins the junior heavyweight title from Kobayashi and praises his strength.
Tenryu wins but gives Misawa credit, and Misawa learns how to fight heavyweights.
Misawa beats Tenryu and announces himself as a heavyweight.
After knee surgery, Misawa moves up to heavyweight and tears off the Tiger Mask in the middle of a match.
With Tenryu gone and AJPW in crisis, Misawa vows to beat Jumbo, who taunts him in a magazine interview.
Misawa takes Jumbo's taunt head-on and trains with Kobashi (no score).
Misawa refuses to be provoked by Jumbo and trains with Kobashi (+2 score).
Misawa tells Kobashi he must get past Jumbo, for the young wrestlers and for AJPW.
Misawa's singles match against Jumbo, the wall he must get over; a win adds 2 to the score.
Jumbo wins and says Misawa still lacks an ace's knack for winning when it counts.
Misawa beats Jumbo, the happiest moment of his career.
Winless in five tries against Hansen, Misawa vows not to challenge him for a year if he loses their Triple Crown match.
Misawa challenges Hansen for the Triple Crown; a win adds 2 to the score.
Hansen keeps the Triple Crown and invites anyone to come and get it.
Misawa finally beats Hansen and says he will accept a rematch.
Hansen's power drives Misawa to train harder than ever.
Misawa's junior Kawada vows to beat him in their next match; Misawa must accept or refuse.
Misawa refuses Kawada, who forms the Seigi Army with Taue; Misawa and Kobashi prepare to face them in a tag match.
Misawa accepts Kawada's challenge and goes straight into their singles match.
Misawa and Kobashi face Kawada and Taue's Seigi Army in a tag match; a win adds 2 to the score.
Misawa's singles match against Kawada, a clash of pride; a win adds 1 to the score.
Kawada and Taue win the tag match, and Misawa vows to pay Kawada back.
Misawa and Kobashi beat Kawada and Taue and credit each other.
Kawada finally beats Misawa, the man he has chased all along.
Misawa beats Kawada and tells him to come back when he has the heart.
After the tag war, Misawa and Kawada head into a singles match to settle things.
Now the man everyone chases, Misawa resolves to fight every match like his life depends on it.
With Jumbo ill and Tenryu gone, Misawa promises Baba to carry AJPW and faces Kobashi in a Triple Crown match.
Misawa defends the Triple Crown against Kobashi; a win adds 2 to the score.
Kobashi wins the Triple Crown and thanks Misawa for getting him there.
Misawa keeps his titles but admits Kobashi was far stronger than he thought.
After match after brutal match, Misawa's body finally gives out.
While Misawa is sidelined, Baba asks him to take over the matchmaking.
Misawa takes on the matchmaking at once to shake AJPW out of its rut (no score).
Misawa asks for time, then takes on the matchmaking and recruits Ogawa (no score).
Misawa teams with junior heavyweight Ogawa to challenge No Fear (Takayama and Omori), the first Triple Crown tag champions.
Misawa and Ogawa challenge Takayama and Omori for the tag titles; a win adds 1 to the score.
Takayama and Omori keep their titles and mock Misawa.
Misawa and Ogawa beat No Fear, and Misawa praises his new partner.
The Ogawa team matures and succeeds, just before an incident that shakes the wrestling world.
After the deaths of Baba and Jumbo, Misawa becomes AJPW president, and Vader, who has beaten the other Four Heavenly Kings, targets him.
Misawa vows to go all out on offense against Vader (+1 score).
Misawa decides to fight a careful match he cannot lose (no score).
Misawa faces Vader, the strongest foreigner; a win adds 2 to the score.
Vader beats Misawa, completing his sweep of the Four Heavenly Kings.
Misawa beats Vader and dedicates the win to Baba.
A year into his presidency, Misawa must choose between AJPW's old spirit and his new wrestling; the story score decides which way he goes.
Misawa stays to protect AJPW, but his half-and-half shows meet resistance from within; the score decides what follows.
Misawa leaves AJPW alone, joins up with Ogawa and Marufuji, and accepts Hashimoto's invitation to fight in ZERO-ONE.
Misawa leaves AJPW with Kobashi and Ogawa and launches the new promotion NOAH.
Kobashi leaves and nearly the whole roster follows; left with only Fuchi, Misawa allies AJPW with NJPW.
Misawa and Kobashi wage a revolution against Kawada's conservative faction and lead an AJPW invasion squad into NJPW.
Freelance Misawa faces Hashimoto in ZERO-ONE; the result does not change the story.
Misawa agrees to bring NOAH to ZERO-ONE's first show alongside Hashimoto.
The historic AJPW-NJPW series opens with Misawa facing NJPW's Kensuke Sasaki.
Misawa's first match in the NJPW ring, against Nakanishi; the result does not change the story.
After his brutal fight with Hashimoto, Misawa accepts a match against the shoot-style fighter Ogawa.
Misawa and Akiyama take on Hashimoto's side in a tag match on ZERO-ONE's first show; the result does not change the story.
Misawa faces Kensuke Sasaki in the series opener; the result does not change the story.
Nakanishi wins on instinct, and Misawa learns the flow of NJPW-style wrestling.
Misawa beats Nakanishi and adapts to NJPW's rhythm.
Misawa faces the shoot-style Ogawa; the result does not change the story.
Hashimoto's side wins, and he vows to settle things with Misawa one-on-one.
Misawa and Akiyama win, though Akiyama doubts it was a dream match.
Sasaki beats Misawa in the historic series opener.
Misawa beats Sasaki in enemy territory.
With the series a hit, Misawa faces Choshu, the series' go-between, in the main event.
Ending: Misawa finds his freedom as a freelancer and charges toward a bigger stage.
As NOAH's president, Misawa must raise the next generation, and rising star Akiyama challenges him for the title.
After the series opener, Tenryu returns to the new AJPW and faces Misawa in the main event.
Misawa faces Choshu in the AJPW-NJPW series main event; the result does not change the story.
Misawa defends his title against Akiyama in a fight for the top of NOAH; the result does not change the story.
Misawa faces the returning Tenryu in the new AJPW's main event; the result does not change the story.
Ending: after the AJPW revolution and the NJPW invasion, Misawa vows to keep leading AJPW toward something new.
Akiyama beats Misawa for the belt and says their fight is only beginning.
Misawa keeps his title and looks forward to more matches with Akiyama.
Ending: left with a rebuilt AJPW, Misawa vows to live by the path he believes in.
A year into NOAH, Misawa talks of breaking down the walls between promotions and of a dream match with Mutoh.
Mutoh leaves NJPW and challenges the head of NOAH, and Misawa defends his GHC title against him.
Misawa defends the GHC title against Mutoh in the dream match; the result does not change the story.
Mutoh wins the dream match and calls Misawa the real deal.
Misawa beats Mutoh and accepts a future rematch.
Ending: NOAH's history has only just begun, and Misawa vows to steer it to an even bigger stage.

Fifteen-year-old Atsushi Onita joins ALL JAPAN, meets Giant Baba and vows to become a huge wrestler like him.
Nine years in, on tour in America, Terry gets Onita an NWA Junior Heavyweight title shot against champion Guerrero.
Match: Onita challenges Chavo Guerrero for the NWA Junior Heavyweight title; a win adds a point, a loss means a later rematch.
Onita lost, but two months later he beats Chavo Guerrero in a rematch and takes the junior title anyway.
Onita returns to Japan as champion, but everyone only wants to talk about NJPW's Tiger Mask; do you go and see him?
Onita buys a ticket to an NJPW show to watch Tiger Mask, causes a ringside scuffle and is suspended for a month.
Onita stays away; Jumbo tells him to just wrestle like a champion, but a strange bad feeling lingers.
During a title defense Onita's left knee shatters; you choose whether he retires, waits for the doctor, or fights on.
Onita accepts that his shattered knee has ended his career and quits pro wrestling.
The diagnosis is a shattered left knee, but Onita refuses to let it end there.
Against Goto's protests Onita begs Baba for a comeback match, but his knee locks up and he has to retire anyway.
Four years on, Onita is a day laborer wondering if there is anything for him besides wrestling; you choose his next step.
Onita almost gives up, then decides it is all up to him and swears to return to wrestling.
Onita decides to make a splash by challenging the shoot-style UWF on his own.
Onita swears he will get back into the wrestling world.
Onita joins Pioneer Go's indie group, buries karate man Takashi Ohashi in his comeback and sets his sights on UWF.
Maeda turns Onita and his challenge away at the door; storm the UWF ring or find another way?
Onita crashes the UWF ring disguised as Super Tiger, provokes the real one and gets a singles match made.
Snubbed by UWF, Onita decides to build his own ring and promotion.
Match: retired, bad-kneed Onita against UWF's Super Tiger; a win adds a point.
At the press conference for his new promotion FMW, Ohashi storms in demanding a rematch, setting up the first show's main event.
After losing to Super Tiger, Onita decides to start his own promotion to make his kind of wrestling real.
Onita's win over Super Tiger wows the press, and he announces on the spot that he is launching a new promotion.
Match: Onita against his grudge rival Takashi Ohashi in FMW's first main event; a win adds a point.
At the press conference for his new promotion FMW, old grudge Ohashi storms in demanding a match, setting up the first show's main event.
FMW's crude first show is a hit, and Onita thanks the crowd from the ring.
To keep FMW alive Onita turns to deathmatches, and his loyal partner Goto vows to make the coming cage deathmatch a success.
Match: the cage deathmatch Goto vowed to make a success (the text does not name the opponent); a win adds a point.
Onita defends FMW's deathmatch path to the press, then Mister Pogo challenges him to a fight to the death.
Match: Onita against Mister Pogo in a deathmatch; a win adds a point.
Battered, Onita tells the press he does it because he loves pro wrestling.
FMW rivals the majors, but Onita is wearing out; he insists on facing Matsunaga in a Barbed Wire Time Bomb Deathmatch anyway.
Match: Barbed Wire Time Bomb Deathmatch against Matsunaga; a win adds a point.
Onita collapses after the match and nearly dies, then prepares for FMW's biggest event, a tag match against Tenryu's Gen-gumi.
Match: Onita's team against Tenryu and his Gen-gumi; winning (+1) keeps him in FMW, losing sends him toward retirement against Choshu.
Worn out after Tenryu, Onita plans to retire and talks Choshu into a straight farewell match.
Onita vows to fight deathmatches as long as his body lasts, but later loses a singles deathmatch to Tenryu.
Match: a normal singles match against Choshu, on condition that Onita retires afterwards; a win adds a point.
His body falling apart, Onita decides to retire for real; the story score now decides how his farewell goes.
Choshu wins and tells Onita to keep his word; Onita bids farewell to FMW.
Onita beats Choshu and announces his retirement to the crowd, satisfied with the greatest match of his life.
FMW sets up an exploding retirement match against Goto, but something unexpected happens.
Onita entrusts FMW to Hayabusa and decides to leave after one final deathmatch with him.
The story score decides what Onita does after his retirement.
Goto refuses to be in Onita's retirement match, and Sasuke rushes in from Sendai to take his place.
Match: Onita's retirement deathmatch against Hayabusa; the result doesn't change the story.
Having lost to Choshu as promised, Onita still wants an exploding farewell match against Goto, but something unexpected happens.
Three years retired and now a lawmaker, Onita announces a comeback and names Antonio Inoki as the man to finish him.
Match: Onita's retirement deathmatch against Sasuke of Michinoku Pro; the result doesn't change the story.
Onita says goodbye to FMW and the fans after six years of deathmatches.
Ignored by Inoki, Onita attacks Shinya Hashimoto in the ZERO-ONE ring and gets a match at 'Ichigeki'.
Onita thanks the fans and the indies and says farewell to pro wrestling.
A year retired, Onita returns for Mister Pogo's retirement match, but FMW's new fans boo him out.
Match: Onita against ZERO-ONE's Shinya Hashimoto as a stepping stone to Inoki; win or lose, the story goes on to Hase.
Three years retired, Onita storms the NJPW ring, headbutts Sasaki and challenges Liger.
Unwelcome in FMW, Onita leaves and declares war on NJPW, naming Choshu as his target.
Hashimoto won, but Onita survived and keeps stalking Inoki, who ignores him completely.
Onita beats Hashimoto and tells the press the Outlaw puts his life on the line.
Liger accepts Onita's challenge and an exploding barbed wire match is booked in NJPW.
Onita invades the NJPW mat, provokes Chono and wins a No-Rope Exploding Barbed Wire Deathmatch at the Dome.
An exhibition between lawmakers Onita and Hase becomes an AJPW 'Dead Serious Showdown' on Onita's old home mat.
Match: exploding barbed wire match against Liger in NJPW; win or lose, AJPW is next.
Match: No-Rope Exploding Barbed Wire Deathmatch against Chono at the Dome; the result doesn't change the story.
Match: the 'Dead Serious Showdown' against Hase in AJPW; the result doesn't change the story.
Liger wins but praises Onita's guts; Onita sets his sights on AJPW.
Onita beats Liger, declares there are no borders in wrestling and names AJPW as his next target.
Having survived Chono, Onita targets IWGP champion Mutoh to force Choshu's hand.
After the Hase match, Onita decides to trick Inoki into a match.
Sasaki vows to kill Onita; Onita breathes fire in his face and an exploding barbed wire match is made.
Onita revives his alter ego Bureido Akkija, sprays mist in Mutoh's face and sets up Akkija vs. Muta.
Onita's secret 'charity exhibition' lures Antonio Inoki to Afghanistan, where Onita is revealed as his opponent.
Match: exploding barbed wire match against Sasaki; the result doesn't change the story.
Match: Onita as Bureido Akkija against Muta in a deathmatch; the result doesn't change the story.
Match: Onita's final match, against Antonio Inoki in Afghanistan; only the post-match scene changes with the result.
Battered after Sasaki, Onita presses on toward the AJPW mat.
Akkija vanishes for good, but Onita survived the IWGP champion and NJPW has no cards left before Choshu.
Inoki wins, and Onita declares the Outlaw died a beautiful death at his hands.
Onita beats Inoki, who demands one more match.
Old friend Fuchi challenges Onita to a plain AJPW-style match with no cage or explosions, and Onita accepts.
Onita shreds Choshu's sweat-soaked T-shirt in the NJPW ring until Choshu agrees to a No-Rope Exploding Barbed Wire Deathmatch.
Ending after the Inoki match: Onita's closing message that a dream is something you grab with your own hands.
Match: a straight AJPW-style match against Fuchi on the ALL JAPAN mat; only the post-match scene changes with the result.
Match: the No-Rope Exploding Barbed Wire Deathmatch against Choshu, the goal of Onita's long road; the result doesn't change the story.
Onita loses to Fuchi in a bout of the year contender and vows to keep charging ahead.
Fuchi admits defeat and concedes Onita is more than an exploding-barbed-wire gimmick.
Choshu calls Onita an idiot but the real deal and takes his hat off to his persistence.
Ending after the Fuchi match: Onita keeps wrestling and urges fans to believe in themselves.
Ending after the Choshu deathmatch: Onita looks back on his unlikely life and says a dream is never out of reach.

Rookie Hashimoto's third day at the NJPW dojo starts with a fight with Chono over the washing machine; asked by Yamamoto to explain, you apologize or blame Chono.
Hashimoto apologizes, but the punishment squats spark another scuffle that pulls in Mutoh, and all three get 3,000 squats (+2 score).
Hashimoto blames Chono, Mutoh gets dragged in, and all three are ordered to do 2,000 squats (no score).
The three rookies become close friends, Hashimoto loses his debut match, and Choshu's Rebel Army walks out; Mutoh calls it a lucky break - do you agree?
Hashimoto agrees it is a chance to make a name, and Mutoh teases him about breaking Sakaguchi's expensive athlete's foot medicine (+1 score).
Hashimoto says the walkout means more responsibility for the young boys, and Mutoh teases him about the broken athlete's foot medicine (+1 score).
With so many seniors gone, Hashimoto admits the young boys came out ahead.
The renamed Young Lion Cup puts Hashimoto, Mutoh and Chono in one league, and Hashimoto names his first opponent Chono as his rival.
Hashimoto's league match against Masahiro Chono; the result changes neither the score nor the story.
Mutoh rises fast while Hashimoto stalls for two years, loses the Young Lion Cup final to Chono and leaves on an overseas tour labeled a demotion.
Called home from Canada by Inoki, Hashimoto is teamed with Mutoh and Chono as the Three War Demons for a one-off six-man tag.
Hashimoto, Chono and Mutoh face Fujinami, Kimura and Koshinaka; the result changes neither the score nor the story.
The Three War Demons' outburst frees Hashimoto's fighting, and two years later he returns home for good as 'the Explosive Crusher.'
After two TKO losses to boxer Tony Halme on a bad knee, Hashimoto trains in China, learns the Leg Sweep and demands a third fight.
Hashimoto's grudge rematch with former boxer Tony Halme; a win adds 2 to the story score, but either result continues the story.
Hashimoto loses again but finally chokes Halme out in a fourth fight to get his revenge.
Hashimoto beats Halme after four long months and feels he has settled the score.
Martial-arts fights have dulled Hashimoto's wrestling, and he must choose: look for a strong opponent or throw himself into training.
Tenryu's WAR invades NJPW, a six-man tag ends in Hashimoto's disqualification, and he stalks Tenryu until he gets a one-on-one match.
Training alone doesn't break the slump, and Hashimoto decides what he really needs is an enemy (+2 score).
Hashimoto faces Genichiro Tenryu for his true comeback; a win adds 2 to the story score, but either result continues the story.
Tenryu praises the bout and says it snapped Hashimoto out of his slump; the two will be rivals.
Hashimoto calls Tenryu amazing and declares himself back and refreshed.
Score check after the Tenryu match: 8 or more leads to an IWGP shot at Mutoh, 4-7 to a Chono feud, under 4 to a title match with the Great Muta.
Hashimoto challenges IWGP champion The Great Muta, and Mutoh's small talk at the dojo calms his nerves before the title match.
Chono angrily interrupts Hashimoto's IWGP plans with a challenge of his own, and Hashimoto accepts the fight.
Hashimoto challenges IWGP champion Keiji Mutoh, whose casual chat about a girl the day before infuriates him.

column3: IWGP Title vs. The Great Muta
column4: Hashimoto challenges The Great Muta for the IWGP title; a win (+1) makes him champion, a loss sends him back to the pack.
Hashimoto fights Masahiro Chono to settle who is stronger; a win adds 1 to the story score, but either result continues the story.
Hashimoto challenges Keiji Mutoh for the IWGP title; a win (+1) makes him champion, a loss sends him back to the pack.
Hashimoto refuses to talk after losing the title match and vows to make it to the top.
Hashimoto wins the IWGP belt, though Mutoh takes it back in his fifth defense.
After a brutal fight with Chono, Liger tells Hashimoto that Choshu has agreed to an interpromotional series with UWF International.
Chono tells Hashimoto that Choshu has agreed to an interpromotional series with UWF International.
When UWF International's Nobuhiko Takada beats Mutoh for the IWGP title, NJPW sends Hashimoto to win it back for the promotion's pride.
Hashimoto challenges Nobuhiko Takada to bring the IWGP belt back to NJPW; a win adds 1 to the story score.

column3: Belt Back at the Second Try
column4: Hashimoto loses, then wins the belt from Takada three months later with a Triangle Choke; a score check (10 or more) decides whether Choshu or Yamazaki challenges next.
Takada admits Hashimoto's hunger for the win was stronger, and the IWGP belt is back in NJPW.
Freelancer Kazuo Yamazaki, inspired by the Takada match, challenges IWGP champion Hashimoto, and Liger warns him to fight it like a shoot.
Rumors call Riki Choshu's IWGP challenge his retirement match; Choshu denies it, and Hashimoto vows to send him off for good.
Hashimoto defends the IWGP title against Kazuo Yamazaki; a win adds 1 to the story score, but either result continues the story.
Hashimoto defends the IWGP title against Riki Choshu; a win adds 1 to the story score, but either result continues the story.
Hashimoto is now NJPW's undisputed top star - until one man's arrival changes his career.
Hashimoto suspects Choshu meant it as a farewell and feels honored; a score of 10 or more brings a challenge from Sasaki first.
The company orders IWGP champion Hashimoto to face Olympic judoka Naoya Ogawa in his debut, and Ogawa's dismissive comments enrage him.
Kensuke Sasaki, angry at how Hashimoto cornered Choshu, attacks him in a tag match and demands a one-on-one fight.
Hashimoto faces debuting Naoya Ogawa in a shoot-style fight; a win adds 2 to the story score.
Hashimoto fights Kensuke Sasaki one-on-one; a win adds 1 to the story score, but either result continues the story.
Hashimoto is beaten by Ogawa, snaps after the match and demands a rematch with the belt on the line.
After two more losses to Ogawa, Hashimoto is ordered to team with him and instead puts his career on the line in a singles match.
Hashimoto faces Naoya Ogawa with his career at stake: a loss means retirement, a win (+2) keeps him in NJPW - the scenario's main fork.
Hashimoto loses and keeps his promise to retire; a score of 15 or more leads to the Tenryu-Kawada route, otherwise the Misawa route.
Hashimoto beats Ogawa, and Inoki enters the ring to tell him the real fight starts now; a score of 15 or more leads to the K-1 war route.
A phone call from NOAH's Misawa and 10,000 fan signatures bring the retired Hashimoto back, determined to go outside NJPW.
Hashimoto turns down Inoki's offer to join UFO, founds ZERO-ONE and, with Tenryu's backing, starts a three-way war with NJPW and AJPW.
Hashimoto brawls with Inoki, Chono threatens to crush him, and his demand that NJPW cut ties with Inoki turns into a fight with President Fujinami.
Le Banner's boasts start a war between K-1 and the Inoki Army, led by Hashimoto, who is ordered to team with Ogawa against Satake and Takada.
Hashimoto's ZERO-ONE announcement and talk of NOAH get him fired from NJPW, and he enters NOAH against Takao Omori.
Hashimoto of ZERO-ONE faces AJPW's Genichiro Tenryu in the three-promotion war; the result changes neither the score nor the story.
Hashimoto fights NJPW president Tatsumi Fujinami to force his demands through; the result changes neither the score nor the story.
Hashimoto and Naoya Ogawa team against Masaaki Satake and Nobuhiko Takada; the result changes neither the score nor the story.
Hashimoto's first NOAH match, against Takao Omori; the result changes neither the score nor the story.
Tenryu praises Hashimoto after their match, and Hashimoto prepares to face AJPW's quiet ace Toshiaki Kawada for ZERO-ONE.
Hashimoto demands Fujinami's presidency, NJPW releases him, and Chono's call-out gets the release put on hold - if Hashimoto fights him.
Hashimoto and Ogawa click as a team, and Le Banner's insults about pro wrestling build up the Inoki Festival main event.
The Omori match gets Hashimoto moving, and ZERO-ONE's launch begins in earnest.
Hashimoto faces AJPW's Toshiaki Kawada in the three-way war main event; the result changes neither the score nor the story.
Hashimoto fights Masahiro Chono to stay in NJPW; the result only changes the post-match scene.
Hashimoto faces K-1's Jerome Le Banner in a mixed-style main event; the result only changes the post-match scene.
For ZERO-ONE's first show against NOAH's Misawa and Akiyama, Yuji Nagata of NJPW volunteers as Hashimoto's mystery partner X.
After the Kawada match, Hashimoto says ZERO-ONE has only just been born.
Hashimoto tells Chono this is only the beginning and vows to take NJPW's top spot.
Hashimoto beats Chono and claims the top spot in NJPW.
Hashimoto has nothing to say and vows to start over from scratch.
A beaten Le Banner has no comment.
Hashimoto and Yuji Nagata face Mitsuharu Misawa and Jun Akiyama at ZERO-ONE's first show; the result changes neither the score nor the story.
Ending of the ZERO-ONE three-way war route: Hashimoto vows, like Nobunaga, to rule the land through pro wrestling.
Ending of the NJPW reform route: Hashimoto vows never to give up chasing his ideal his own way.
Kazuyuki Fujita beats Le Banner, his 'stole my lunch' remark goes to press, and Hashimoto calls out the double IWGP champion.
Ogawa wrecks ZERO-ONE's first show, Misawa cuts ties, and after two years building ZERO-ONE Hashimoto finally gets Misawa one-on-one.
Hashimoto fights Kazuyuki Fujita to settle who is stronger; the result changes neither the score nor the story.
Hashimoto faces Mitsuharu Misawa one-on-one in the ZERO-ONE vs. NOAH war; the result only changes the post-match scene.
Ending of the Inoki Army vs. K-1 route: Hashimoto says fighting is the only way he can express himself.
Hashimoto refuses to accept the loss and demands another match with Misawa.
Misawa admits a clean loss to Hashimoto's finish.
Ending of the ZERO-ONE vs. NOAH route: Hashimoto resolves to keep charging ahead and live as a warrior.

Chono recalls brutal NJPW dojo training, Mutoh's fake escape plan, Hashimoto's antics, and his vow to out-train the two rivals who joined with him.
Choshu's walkout opens debut spots, and three years later Chono reaches the Young Lion Cup final against Hashimoto.
Match 0: Chono faces Shinya Hashimoto in the Young Lion Cup final; a win adds 1 to the story score.
Chono loses the final, curses Hashimoto's kicks, but is satisfied he gave everything.
Chono wins the Young Lion Cup; a furious Hashimoto swears revenge.
Sakaguchi sends Chono on an overseas excursion and lets him pick where to go: Austria, Germany or Canada.
Chono suffers in gloomy European rings, is crushed by the giant Vader, then finds his feet in Canada with friends nearby.
Chono trains in Canada with Mutoh and Hashimoto close by, then moves to Europe and is crushed by the giant Vader.
Now one of the Three War Demons, Chono learns his first Tokyo Dome opponent is Vader, before 50,000 fans.
Match 1: Chono faces Vader at the Dome; a win adds 1 to the score, but the story continues the same either way.
Chono barely remembers the frantic Vader fight but now has the guts for the big stage.
Back in Japan, Chono and Hashimoto both challenge Inoki, and Sakaguchi books them as a team against Inoki and himself.
Chono swallows his pride and agrees to team with Hashimoto.
Chono asks for Inoki one-on-one, Sakaguchi refuses, and Chono accepts any partner out of spite.
Inoki slaps a reporter and vows to win; Chono vows to make the generational change official.
Match 2: Chono and Hashimoto face Antonio Inoki and Sakaguchi; a win adds 2 to the score.
Inoki wins a close call and leads his 1-2-3 Daa; Chono vows to beat him one day.
Chono and Hashimoto beat their master Inoki for the first time and dare anyone to stop them.
Overlooked by the press, Chono upsets Choshu and Hashimoto with the STF to reach the first G1 Climax final against Mutoh.
